title: Staff Offensive Security Engineer, Proactive threat
description: Who we are About Stripe Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career. About the team The Proactive Threat team finds vulnerabilities and security weaknesses across Stripe's systems, applications, networks, and cloud infrastructure before adversaries do. We're a hybrid offensive function. We run penetration tests, emulate real-world threat actors in red team operations, and work closely with our defensive security teams to validate detection capabilities and improve Stripe's overall security posture. We are builders first. We build custom tooling, automation frameworks, and internal platforms that scale our offensive work and make our assessments repeatable and high-fidelity. Increasingly, that includes AI agents that find and validate vulnerabilities at a scale no human team could reach. We believe the best offensive security engineers are equal parts hacker and engineer. The team is distributed and works regularly with security, engineering, and product stakeholders across Stripe, including teams in Europe and Asia. What you'll do As a Staff Offensive Security Engineer on the Proactive Threat team, you'll set the technical direction for how Stripe tests itself the way a real adversary would. You'll be the team's most senior offensive practitioner. You'll stay deeply hands-on: you'll lead the hardest engagements yourself and write the tooling that makes everyone around you more effective. You'll own the strategy and the operating foundation of our red team program, including its tradecraft, infrastructure, rules of engagement, and coordination with detection and response. You'll shape how offensive security scales at Stripe through automation and agentic systems. Your work will span multiple teams: you'll partner with detection engineering, incident response, vulnerability management, and product engineering so that what we find makes Stripe measurably harder to attack. Responsibilities Technical strategy and leadership Set the multi-quarter technical strategy for offensive security at Stripe: where we test, how deep we go, and which threat actors and attack paths matter most to a financial infrastructure company Define and own the red team program's operating foundation: rules of engagement, opsec standards, C2 and payload infrastructure, IR deconfliction, and repeatable engagement playbooks Be the prime mover on large, ambiguous offensive initiatives that span multiple teams, from framing the problem to landing the outcome Make fast, well-reasoned calls on scope, risk, and tradecraft, and explain them clearly to engineers, security leaders, and executives Hands-on offensive work Lead the team's most complex engagements yourself: objective-based red team operations, assumed-breach exercises, and deep assessments of critical payment, money-movement, cloud, CI/CD, and corporate systems Emulate the TTPs of sophisticated cyber and criminal threat actors targeting financial services, including initial access, lateral movement, persistence, and data exfiltration Find novel vulnerability classes and attack chains specific to Stripe's architecture, and turn them into systemic fixes rather than one-off findings Scaling through engineering and automation Design and build the offensive platforms, tooling, and agentic workflows that encode the team's expertise into repeatable, scalable systems Apply LLMs and autonomous agents to reconnaissance, vulnerability discovery, exploit validation, and reporting, and set the bar for running them safely and reliably Raise the engineering quality of the team's codebases through design reviews, code reviews, and example Cross-team impact Partner with detection engineering, threat intelligence, and incident response to run purple team operations, close detection gaps, and measure improvement over time Work with vulnerability management and product engineering teams so findings lead to durable, systemic remediation Help manage external offensive vendors and partners by setting scope, holding them to a quality bar, and integrating their results with our own work Act as the subject-matter expert on adversary behavior for Stripe-wide security initiatives, incident investigations, and leadership decisions Multiplying the team Mentor and grow offensive security engineers at all levels, and raise the team's technical bar through pairing, design review, and knowledge sharing Shape hiring for the team, including interview design and calibration Represent Stripe in the broader security community through research, talks, and open-source contributions where appropriate Who you are We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement. Minimum requirements 8+ years of experience in offensive security, penetration testing, red teaming, or a related field, including significant time as a technical lead on complex engagements A track record of setting technical direction for an offensive security program or capability, with impact across multiple teams Strong software engineering skills in Python, Go, or similar languages, with a history of designing and shipping production-quality offensive tools, platforms, or automation that others rely on Expert knowledge of adversary tradecraft and frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK, and experience planning and running full-scope red team operations, including C2 infrastructure, opsec, and deconfliction with defenders Deep, hands-on expertise in
